record_verbatim.calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic. They describe the hypothetical Project Northcell as its own artefact says that programme does not exist. No date here is a real commitment, a real gate date or a real review date.

changes_made.adoption_evidence: The check is described in FB2-SUP-QAP-000001's acceptance criteria. It has been performed once, in this authoring pass, against FB2-SAF-SGO-000001.
changes_made.change: Add to the review checklist an arithmetic check that sums each timing budget's serial elements and margin and compares the total with the stated fault-tolerant time interval

counter_evidence: The check was applied to exactly one record. A search for other timing budgets in the corpus was run and found none, so there is no second application to compare against.
The change did not prevent the error; it found it after the fact. The safety goal was baselined with the error in it and remains baselined with it.

The improvement is recorded by the same role that authored the records it criticises, so it has no independence. A real programme would require the evaluation to be performed by a party who did not write the budget.

effectiveness_evaluation.arithmetic: Before: 1 record fails (FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 at 105 ms against 100 ms). After: 0 NEW records fail; the technical safety concept FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 declares 85 ms serial plus 15 ms margin = 100 ms and closes exactly. 1 - 1 = 0 new failures. The pre-existing failure is NOT counted as fixed: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 still does not close and cannot be edited without a controlled change.
effectiveness_evaluation.confirmation_by_second_role: reviewer_adversarial (fictional role identity). The confirmation pass disagreed with a 'partially_effective' verdict only in that it held the non-verdict should be 'insufficient_evidence'; the recorded verdict was left at partially_effective and the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved by picking one.
effectiveness_evaluation.verdict_argument: The check works on the record it was run against: it found the error and the new record written under it closes. It is not demonstrably effective, because the only evidence is one application to one record, and one application cannot distinguish a working check from a lucky read. It is also not a fix: the original record is still wrong.

hypothesis.falsification_condition: If a second timing budget that does not close is written after the check is adopted and is not caught by it, the hypothesis is false and the check is ineffective.
hypothesis.predicted_effect: The number of timing budget records whose arithmetic does not close will fall from 1 to 0 for records written after the check is adopted.
hypothesis.statement: Adding a review check that computes each timing budget's arithmetic and compares it with the interval will cause a budget that does not close to be found at review time rather than at concept-writing time.
